note: EXPERIMENTAL; rigid boxes are PRESCRIBED from the ground-truth trajectory (teacher-forced obstacles); only the soft-body vertices are predicted.
seed_note: rollouts are seeded with the true frames (0, 1) and predict frames 2..T

physics_reference.description: PyBullet ground truth scored with the same metrics (floor for penetration / strain)

hold_initial.description: trivial baseline: the last seeded frame is held

rigid_freefall.description: trivial baseline: rigid free-fall of the seeded shape (COM velocity + gravity) until the table top / floor (+ --baseline-clearance, the collision margin), then stop

soft_raw.description: SoftGNN alone: learned model only, no projection

soft_projected.description: SoftGNN + non-learned project_soft after every step

soft_projected_margin.description: SoftGNN + project_soft keeping vertices one collision margin outside surfaces

soft_projected_sleep.description: SoftGNN + project_soft + NON-LEARNED sleep rule (a supported body whose vertices all move less than --sleep-move per step is held in place)

notes: EXPERIMENTAL research prototype. rigid boxes are PRESCRIBED from the ground-truth trajectory (teacher-forced obstacles); only the soft-body vertices are predicted in every engine.
COM is the unweighted mean of the soft vertices; shape error removes each trajectory's COM translation (no rotation alignment).

Penetration and strain error are averaged over the predicted frames only; physics_reference shows what the ground truth itself scores (PyBullet soft nodes hover about one collision margin above surfaces, so its penetration is near zero).
The penetration column is the mean vertex depth with each vertex capped at 50 mm (one fall-through rollout cannot dominate); the JSON also holds the uncapped mean.
final-rest COM error is the last-frame COM error over episodes whose ground truth is at rest at the last frame.

Pinned (kinematic) vertices, if the data has any, are prescribed from the ground truth in the model engines and count in the vertex means (with zero error there); the trivial baselines do not move them either way.
CPU ms/step: batch 1, first episode of the split (64 vertices), 8 torch threads, float32, median over 40 autoregressive steps.

example.selection: median final-frame vertex error of soft_projected
